title: AI Native SW Engineering Consultant
description: You build the systems that actually make AI work in enterprise environments, not demos, not prototypes that stall after a pilot, but production agentic architectures running inside real client organizations. The difference between an AI Engineer and what we are looking for is straightforward: you have shipped a multi\-agent system in production, you have owned the eval harness, and you know what happens when your agent fails at 2am because you have lived it. As an AI Engineer (Agentic/Applied), you will design, build, and deploy production\-grade agentic AI systems across the full enterprise technology stack. You will work directly with client engineering teams, lead technical design sessions, and build reusable patterns and accelerators that scale beyond individual engagements. This role sits at the heart of the AI engineering talent market — demand is growing faster than supply and will continue to do so. We offer what no single product company can: breadth across every industry, every enterprise technology stack, and every level of organizational complexity, combined with vendor fellowship access inside Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google engineering teams and a direct pathway to the Forward Deployed Engineer programme. **Key Responsibilities** - Design and build production\-grade agentic systems end\-to\-end: multi\-agent orchestration, RAG pipelines, policy\-based routing, tool invocation, memory management, and lifecycle observability - Build and own RAG pipelines: embeddings, chunking strategy, vector search, context window engineering and tuning against real quality targets - Integrate and abstract across multiple LLM providers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Vertex AI, and open\-source models — with fallback routing, token, cost, and latency management - Implement LLMOps in production: eval harnesses with real quality metrics, prompt versioning, observability tooling (LangSmith, Braintrust, or equivalent), cost and safety monitoring - Embed directly with client engineering teams to design, prototype, and deploy agentic solutions — workshops, proofs of concept, code\-with sessions, and architecture walkthroughs - Build reusable patterns, accelerators, and playbooks that scale beyond the individual client engagement and enable the next one to start faster - Define and use metrics to measure agent accuracy, latency, safety, and cost\-effectiveness; present findings and recommendations to client stakeholders in business terms - Software engineering experience in production environments - Minimum 1 year of hands\-on experience designing and deploying agentic AI solutions in a production environment — non\-negotiable - Demonstrated experience with agentic orchestration frameworks: LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or equivalent — at production depth, not tutorial level - Direct experience calling LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Vertex AI) in production code: provider abstraction, token management, latency and cost tradeoffs - RAG pipeline ownership: embeddings, chunking strategy, vector databases, and context engineering - LLMOps fundamentals: eval harness design, prompt versioning, and production observability - Cloud\-native engineering maturity: Kubernetes, Docker, microservices, serverless, CI/CD, and IaC (Terraform or Helm) - Strong Python; Java or equivalent backend language acceptable; production debugging and observability experience - Quality of experience is weighted over years, a candidate who has shipped three production agentic systems in four years is preferred over a generalist with passive AI exposure

title: Associate Interior Designer
description: Ruumi Studio is an architecture and interior design practice with studios in Dublin and Manchester, and a presence in London. We began in early 2026 as a spin\-out from an international real estate firm, and we brought our live portfolio and our design IP with us. It meant we skipped the year most new practices spend chasing work. We opened with a full order book and it has stayed full. In our first year we have delivered over 250,000 sq ft and been nominated for four awards so far this year. Around half our work is commercial fit\-out. A quarter is heritage and deep retrofit. The balance runs across aviation, industrial and workplace. The interiors work here is not decoration applied at the end of an architectural process. It is the project. We own a furniture dealership. This changes the job. Indi is our furniture dealership, and it sits inside the group. We hold the manufacturer relationships directly, on our own terms, with the trading account in our name. For a designer, that means several things that are unusual in this market. You can specify having actually sat in the thing. You can get a sample in the studio in days rather than negotiating with somebody else’s rep. You can hold a real conversation about lead time, price and substitution at the point of specification instead of discovering the problem at tender. And when a client’s budget moves, you have commercial room to move with it rather than starting the schedule again. The obvious question is whether that means you will be pushed to specify in\-group product. No. The dealership serves the design work, not the other way round. If the right answer is a manufacturer we do not represent, we specify it. A practice that lets the trading account drive the specification is not a design practice, it is a sales operation with drawings. Lad Lane We move into a new studio on Lad Lane in September. Two floors of a self\-contained mews, with the Indi showroom on the ground floor. Your samples and your specification library will be one staircase away, and you will have a hand in what goes into the space. We designed it ourselves, which seemed like the minimum standard for a practice that spends its days telling other organisations how their workplace should perform. It is not, on the evidence of visiting our competitors, an industry norm. The nine\-day fortnight Every second Friday off, from your first day. Not a pilot, not something you earn after probation. The reasoning is unromantic. This industry has a well\-documented habit of consuming people at exactly the point they become properly good at the job. We would rather not, and then congratulate ourselves on the overtime. What we ask for Two things, and neither is negotiable. Revit proficiency. Not “familiar with”. If your workflow is currently SketchUp and hope, this is not the right role. You can model, detail and coordinate without somebody standing behind you. An inquisitive mind. The sort of person who disappears down a rabbit hole on a Friday afternoon and comes back knowing how something works, or why a material behaves the way it does. That is the list. We will teach the rest. What helps • Commercial office, workplace or fit\-out experience. It is the bulk of what we do. • FF\&E specification experience, and opinions about it. You will have more influence over specification here than at most practices, so bring some. • You are already augmenting your design or documentation workflow with AI. We are building the practice around this rather than waiting to see how it settles. • Comfort working with existing and historic building fabric. A quarter of our work involves buildings that push back. • Professional membership is welcome but not required. There is no register for interior design in Ireland and we are not going to pretend there is a proxy for talent. Pay Senior / Associate: €58,000 to €78,000 Bands are set by capability, not by years served. What matters is what you can run unsupervised, what you can specify with authority, and what you can hold in front of a client. Where you land in a band follows from that rather than from how comfortable you are asking. Some people find that conversation easy and some find it excruciating, and we would rather pay for the work than for the confidence. What you get • The nine\-day fortnight, as above. • Real responsibility on live projects, early. • Direct access to the directors, and to the manufacturers. • At senior and associate level, a defined leadership pathway that ends in a position of real responsibility across both the studio and the dealership. There is more than one way to build a career here and we would rather be explicit about that now. • We submit our B Corp application in Q1 2027, once we have a full year of trading behind us. Not certified yet, and we will not pretend otherwise. Practical Lad Lane, Dublin 2\. Hybrid, minimum three days a week in the studio. Before you apply At a practice this size you can find out exactly who you would be working with before you send anything. That is harder to do with a hundred\-person studio, where you meet whoever is free on the day. One of our co\-founders was on Architecture Social recently, talking about how Ruumi is run, how we build around AI and what we actually look for when hiring. It was not recorded with recruitment in mind, which is rather the point. https://open.spotify.com/episode/7o1RoOQ1gXHaBPZi5Jftdd To apply CV and portfolio to www.ruumi.studio/careers. title: Commissioning Engineer
description: Covering Leinster As Commissioning Engineer, you will work as part of our multi\-disciplinary engineering team to bring water and wastewater projects from installation completion through all stages of commissioning into operation and ultimate handover to our clients. You will have the opportunity to work alongside and collaborate with industry\-leading project teams, working in a one\-team culture while broadening your own skill set. As Commissioning Engineer, you will demonstrate our core values including innovation and agility. In this client\-facing role, you will be key to the final sign\-off and handover to the client in a collaborative and satisfactory manner. Glanua is a progressive company which always seeks to develop its employees. When you demonstrate aptitude and interest in furthering your career within the organisation, training and promotion will always be available to you. **Main Duties and Responsibilities:** The main duties and responsibilities of the Commissioning Engineer are outlined as follows: * Work as part of a team in the delivery of one or more projects at any one time, embracing the ethos of a “one team” culture. * Ensure Health, Safety, Environmental \& Sustainability standards, policies and procedures are always adhered to on\-site. * Support project delivery teams in the development and preparation of commissioning test documentation. * Review of design stage control philosophies, motor and instrument listings, panel drawings and cable schedules in order to validate designs, familiarise with project and spot issues before they arise. * Attend Hazard and Operability Studies (HAZOP) and Control Hazard and Operability studies (CHAZOP) and provide input on commissioning and operability issues as required. * Attend third part Factory Acceptance Tests (FATs) and Site Acceptance Tests (SATs) as required and provide acceptance sign\-off on behalf of the company. * Complete preliminary installation checks and provide completion snag lists to mechanical and electrical sub\-contractors. * Conduct initial power\-up of MCC’s and complete rotation checks on motors and I/O point\-to\-point checks (dry testing). * Set up instrumentation in the field and scale instrument 4\-20 mA signals back to PLC. Calibrate any instruments requiring field calibration. * Upload the first draft of the PLC code in conjunction with the automation engineer and conduct preliminary dry tests. * Divert flows to new works process and conduct wet testing of PLC/HMI/SCADA automated sequences. Ensure that PLC/HMI/SCADA logic conforms to control philosophy and de\-bug as necessary. * Troubleshoot equipment, instrumentation, hardware, and software in order to ensure correct operation. * Work with Process Engineers in order to optimise and improve the process performance of water and wastewater infrastructure. * Complete all commissioning documentation including pre\-test inspections, commissioning reports and works demonstration. Provide demonstration of same to client and receive sign\-off. * Liaise closely with the project delivery engineering team on\-site, HSQE advisor, and management in order to ensure safe and timely delivery of the commissioning process. * Organise and facilitate plant shutdowns and/or diversion of flows as required with project delivery team and the client through permit\-to\-work systems. * Ensure a positive experience for the client and their representatives instilling an ethos of collaboration and cooperation. * Seek to improve the commissioning process by providing lessons learned feedback and innovative solutions for adoption on future projects. * Keep appraised of the latest standards and technology through continuous professional development (CPD). * Other duties as required from time to time. **Knowledge, Skills and Experience:** The main knowledge, skills and experience required of the Commissioning Engineer are outlined as follows: * Minimum of 3 years’ experience working in a similar role, preferably in the water and wastewater industry. * Experienced in the commissioning and process proving of mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, control and automation (MEICA) systems. * Ability to liaise directly with customers on commissioning activities and sign\-off. * Relevant Electrical Qualification. * Ability to work as part of a team with excellent communication and interpersonal skills. * Ability to make PLC/HMI modifications desirable. * Ability to manage time in a pressurised environment during commissioning process. * Ability to use own initiative, problem solve and adjust as issues arise during commissioning. * Good working knowledge of MS packages such as Word and Excel. * Full Driving License. **What we offer you:** The opportunity to join an ambitious and growing organisation. * Monday to Friday working week finishing early on Fridays. * 22 days annual leave plus 10 bank holidays. * A company laptop and phone. * Fully expensed company vehicle * Access to EAP – 24/7 365 days confidential employee counselling service, free to avail for employees and their families

title: EDA Tooling, Release & Sign-off Engineer
description: We Are: At Synopsys, we drive the innovations that shape how we live and connect. Logic\-engineering know\-how (synthesis, STA, and similar) is a welcome bonus rather than a prerequisite. What You’ll Be Doing: * Own and execute the product release process for complex soft IP: assemble and package deliverables, verify that contents and configurations are complete and correct, and produce clean release collateral. * Run release testing and sign\-off: exercise release regressions and quality gates, confirm the product is packaged correctly, and sign off deliverables before they ship to customers and downstream teams. * Develop, run, and maintain EDA tooling, flow automation, and project infrastructure (Tcl/Python/Make\-based), plus dashboards that track release status and quality. * Debug tooling and release failures end to end: analyze logs and reports, isolate root cause, communicate status and risks clearly, and drive issues to closure with design, verification, and implementation teams. * Apply AI to accelerate the work (e.g., triaging flow and release logs, summarizing regression and QoR trends, drafting and refactoring scripts). * Improve documentation, packaging and sign\-off criteria, and reusable collateral so releases stay consistent and repeatable across IP programs. * Bonus: contribute to mid\-end logic flows — synthesis, DFT, static checking (SpyGlass), formal equivalence, and power analysis — where it supports release readiness. The Impact You Will Have: * Products released on time, packaged correctly, and signed off with confidence. * Faster, more scalable execution through stronger automation and AI\-enabled analysis. * Packaging, release, and quality\-gate issues caught earlier in the cycle. * Tighter collaboration and clearer communication across the design\-to\-release chain. * Robust, implementation\-ready soft IP shipped with clear collateral, checks, and sign\-off. What You’ll Need (Core): * Working knowledge of EDA tooling and flow/automation development, typically gained through 2\+ years of relevant experience or equivalent project work. * Experience with — or strong aptitude for — product release and sign\-off: packaging deliverables, running release regressions, and verifying content and quality gates. * Good scripting skills (Tcl and/or Python) and a practical, automation\-first mindset. * Comfort with build/packaging systems, revision control (e.g., Perforce or Git), and regression/CI flows. * Enough understanding of ASIC design and verification flows to support and debug the tooling around them. * Ability to use AI tools effectively to accelerate debugging, summarize results, and improve scripts and flows. * Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarize issues, explain release status and risks, and align cross\-functional teams on next steps * BS/MS in Electrical/Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience. Nice to have (Bonus): * Hands\-on logic engineering: synthesis, static timing analysis (STA), DFT, static checking (SpyGlass), formal equivalence (e.g., Formality), or power analysis. * Hands\-on with Synopsys tools such as Fusion Compiler, VC SpyGlass, or Formality. * IP development methodologies, IP packaging, or reusable IP delivery / release collateral. * Experience building CI/CD pipelines, regression frameworks, or reporting dashboards. Who You Are: * Proactive, curious, and adaptable. * Collaborative, communicative, and ethical. * Flow\-oriented, AI\-aware, and quality focused. * Resilient and results oriented. The Team You’ll Be A Part Of: You’ll work with a high\-impact High\-Performance\-Compute team focused on delivering complex IP to the marketplace. You will collaborate across RTL design, verification, DFT, physical design, methodology, and project infrastructure teams to improve mid\-end readiness and enable predictable downstream implementation. Rewards and Benefits: We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Your recruiter will provide more details about salary and benefits during the hiring process.

Additional benefits include employer pension contributions, a funded CARE allowance for clinical cases, and discounted veterinary care for your own pets. Relocation support is also available for those moving to the area. **A Role You Can Grow Into** This is a fantastic opportunity to join a well\-established and supportive practice where you can develop your skills, enjoy real clinical variety, and build strong relationships with your clients. title: R&D Firmware Engineer
description: At **ABB** , we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. We are seeking a **Firmware Engineer** with a strong understanding of embedded systems design to join our team. In this role, you will contribute to the development of next\-generation sensors, measurement platforms, and actuators, working collaboratively within cross\-functional engineering teams to bring innovative products to market. As part of ABB, you’ll join a truly global organisation at the forefront of sustainable industrial technology. Here, your work creates impact you can see and feel, every day. **Your Role And Responsibilities** In this role, you’ll help run what runs the world, by taking on meaningful work that drives real impact. * Work model: onsite from our Dundalk location {} * Develop and maintain robust, scalable firmware solutions for next\-generation products. * Design, implement, and integrate measurement and control algorithms on embedded platforms. * Produce high\-quality firmware designs, code, and technical documentation. * Collaborate with cross\-functional teams, project managers, and stakeholders to deliver project objectives. * Work within an Agile/Scrum environment, providing accurate estimates, planning, and progress updates. * Troubleshoot, diagnose, and resolve firmware and system issues throughout the product lifecycle. * Support customers and manufacturing teams by investigating and resolving technical challenges. * Evaluate emerging technologies and contribute innovative ideas to enhance the product portfolio. **Qualifications For The Role** * Bachelor’s degree in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline, with working experience in firmware development. * Strong Embedded C/C\+\+ programming skills and experience developing firmware for embedded systems. * Experience writing low\-level PCB drivers, board bring\-up activities, and working directly with hardware, schematics, and electronics. * Knowledge of microcontrollers (e.g., STM32, Cortex\-M) and peripherals including USB, UART, SPI, I²C, Timers, and PWM. * Experience with real\-time operating systems (RTOS), data acquisition, signal processing, and industrial communication protocols such as Modbus\-RTU and RS232/RS485\. * Understanding of networking concepts and implementation of TCP/IP and UDP communications. * Proficiency with development and debugging tools such as Visual Studio, IAR, and Lauterbach, alongside strong troubleshooting and test design skills. * Excellent communication and teamwork skills, a passion for problem\-solving and continuous learning; exposure to C\# development and UML design tools is advantageous. **Benefits** ABB offers a full range of benefits to help you thrive at work and beyond. * Competitive salary * Private Medical Allowance for yourself and family * Competitive contributory Pension Scheme * Employee Share Acquisition Plan * Internal mobility opportunities, mentorships \& access to projects globally * Employee Assistance Programme * Generous employee referral scheme * 25 days Annual Leave plus Bank Holidays **More About Us** *The Process Industries Division serves the mining, minerals processing, metals, cement, pulp and paper, battery manufacturing, and food and beverage, as well as their associated service industries. For mining, metals and cement customers, solutions include specialized products and services, as well as total production systems. Digitalization solutions, including collaborative operations and augmented reality, help improve plant and enterprise productivity, and reduce maintenance and energy costs.* Join us. Run What Runs the World. \#RunwithABB Building a cleaner, smarter future takes all kinds of minds: the curious, the courageous, and the creative.
